results.title: What's new in buddylist: the changelog
results.content:
Start a contact with a team — Settings > Teams keeps roles, agents with a name, a service, a model, an effort level and rules of their own, and teams of them. Pick a team under Team in Add a Contact, and its roles join the new conversation right away. The app starts with a Reviewer: a read-only Claude that waits until another agent has changed files, looks them over and hands back what has to change, then looks again once it is fixed.
 Code in colour — Diffs in the Changes tab and code blocks in replies are coloured by their language: keywords, strings, comments and names each in a colour of their own, on the green and red of added and removed lines. A minified file, or one with a line over 1,000 characters, stays plain. [...] ## v0.2.1

 Inspect uncommitted files and diffs in the Changes tab beside a conversation.
 See merged pull requests, merge conflicts and check status in the contact list.
 Let contacts choose effort levels automatically for messages and group conversations.
 Contacts are grouped by project by default, with clearer worktree progress and faster contact removal.

## v0.2.0

 First public packaged release for Apple Silicon Macs.
 Chat with Claude Code, Codex, Gemini and OpenCode through a classic messenger buddy list using your own agent accounts.

All downloads on GitHub [...] Mention a file with @ — Type @ in the message box for a list of the files in the contact's folder, and keep typing a name or part of its path to narrow it. Choose with the arrow keys and Enter or Tab. In a group conversation the agents come first. Files Git ignores are left out, and paths with spaces are quoted for you.
 Attach files from the message box — The + among the tools under the message box opens the Send Files picker in the contact's folder. An empty message box now reminds you of @ for files and, where the agent has them, / for commands.
 Suggested replies for Codex — When Codex ends a turn by asking you something, replies to click come up under it, as they do for Claude. Settings > General > Suggest replies turns them off for both.
